body:
# Independent audit: perspective-coupled projective erosion

Source:
`candidate c56743c8d6824a18`.

Result: PASS, no substantive correction identified. The exact midpoint
compatibility and literal loss accounting are proved; a Gamma payment
for the entire coupled family is correctly not claimed.

## 1. Exact contact compatibility

After the stated interior-center translations, all support heights are
positive and bounded away from zero. Weighted Jensen uses the weights
h_A/(h_A+h_B), h_B/(h_A+h_B), whose averaged argument is exactly
1+a.(x+x')/2. Thus the averaged input field is at least the middle
perspective field, with the correct factor h_M. The input inequalities
then give their midpoint in M_e, and g_K<=g_M gives M_e subset K_e.
This is a finite-time inclusion for all normals and all actual input
points, not merely a first-order contact test.

The prescribed source's membership in int M is explicit and sufficient
for the interior endpoint decomposition. It is not inferred from being
a mixed deepest point. Adding another nonnegative convex field to an
input only shrinks it and preserves the inclusion, as claimed.

## 2. Continuum-normal first variation

The uniform bound on Psi/h and positivity prove
(1-Ce)L subset L_e subset L. At a boundary ray x, every baseline active
normal gives the lower bound on delta_e in(10). A maximizing perturbed
normal exists by compactness. Its old support ratio tends to one; from
the exact endpoint equation its delta_e is at most its perturbed field
ratio divided by that old support ratio. Every limit normal is active,
so the claimed maximum and limit follow. This also covers a nonsmooth
normal cone; selecting an arbitrary member instead would be wrong.

The radial map and its inverse are Lipschitz because the inradius is
positive. Unique-normal surface-almost-everywhere therefore transfers to
sphere-almost-everywhere. The uniform radial loss bound provides the
dominating integrand. The cone area identity then yields exactly the
surface integral, with no missing support-height factor. The d=1
counting version has the same derivation.

Proper fixed cuts have surface-null intersections with their cutting
plane. Their radial indicators consequently converge almost everywhere.
The separate supporting full/empty cases are essential and correct:
an outside closed supporting facet has zero d-volume loss, even though
its closed boundary indicator has positive surface measure. Pure integer
traces are correctly retained through these full/empty formulas.

## 3. Cost, original cap slices, and affine calibration

The source total D_K and both input totals are all included. Every
ambient cap uses its actual restrictions at all three bases; the inputs
are not replaced by cuts through their own chosen centers. Additive
input fields give additive first losses on that same boundary by the
proved formula, with no double counting of source roles.

At a=0 every evaluated argument is1 and every field is its support
height. The exact maps are common-ratio homotheties about an affine
center graph. Formula(18) is an invertible lattice-preserving ambient
affine map and scales every fiber volume equally, so normalized maximum
depth is unchanged for every e<1. For a regular critical fixed cap,
pullback under this map is a differentiable family of caps through the
same fixed source. Its derivative vanishes at the cap minimum, giving
the exact loss dQ. This independent argument confirms the section-moment
calculation and its tilt correction.

For the stated radii, Q=6, M=5409/400, total loss5409/200 and row loss12
all check. The own loss9 and own cap loss4 show precisely how compatible
input cost lowers the combined efficiency to800/1803. This is a genuine
critical example but remains above OC; the source states that scope.

The further nonlinear source-parameter problem is separate. Near a=0
one may use a fixed positive tangent cutoff below all actual denominator
ranges, but a moving or active cutoff must be retained in any global
second-order calculation.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
